📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

According to recent reports, the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

It has been revealed that the best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman mentioned. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Industry observers note that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Sources indicate that she told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

It has been revealed that “My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson claims. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

It has been revealed that “My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

Industry observers note that the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

In a recent development, toone promptly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven massive-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:18.

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their excellent run of form when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday evening.

Los Blancos will enter the league fixture off the back of a thumping 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

Jose Mourinho's side have now won each of their last 10 matches in all competitions, including their last six fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Real Madrid beat Celta Vigo 2-1 in the league last time out, and they presently sit second in the La Liga table, three points behind the leaders Barcelona.

Alaves, meanwhile, have been one of the success stories in La Liga this season, picking up 16 points from 13 matches, which has left them in ninth spot in the table.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up the head-to-head record and looks at the previous meetings between the two teams ahead of their clash in the Spanish capital.

Real Madrid have tackled Alaves on 46 occasions throughout history, and unsurprisingly, the Madrid giants lead the overall head-to-head record with 38 wins to Alaves five, while there have only ever been three draws between the two teams.

Karim Benzema is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having scored nine times against Alaves during his time at Real Madrid.

Real Madrid are on 121 goals against Alaves, conceding just 34, and Los Blancos are on a nine-game winning run against the Basque side.

That said, Alaves do have a recent famous win over Real Madrid to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory when the two teams locked horns at Bernabeu in November 2020, thanks to goals from Lucas Perez and Joselu.

Alaves have beaten Real Madrid only twice since 2000, though, while there has not been a draw between the two sides since October 2001.

Two of Alaves' five wins over Los Blancos have actually come at the Bernabeu, also triumphing 1-0 in the famous stadium back in 2000.

In La Liga, the teams have met on 40 occasions, with Real Madrid winning 34 times to Alaves' four, drawing twice in the process.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • In a sport obsessed with the next significant thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.
  • The latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 25 November 2026.

In a sport obsessed with the next significant thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

The latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

According to recent reports, of course, injuries, personal problems and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night.

In 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

The hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

In a recent development, but things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

Recent findings suggest that after making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

From that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential.

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

He had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

Industry observers note that since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

According to recent reports, morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is right now plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy.

It has been revealed that the first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

It has been revealed that however, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

Recent findings suggest that but his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

The Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

It has been revealed that robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

According to recent reports, the Brazilian is at the moment imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil.

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

It has been revealed that mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

The hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

In a recent development, but the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

The Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top.

From one player who never indicated his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the significant transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a big-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos.

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

In a recent development, the Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries.

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

The Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

It has been revealed that after six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

Back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

According to recent reports, it seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral.

Sources indicate that after a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

In a recent development, two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

Industry observers note that kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career.

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is said and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

Torino vs Lazio - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (677 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:23.
  • Still leading the pack in Serie A, surprise Scudetto challengers Lazio will visit mid-table Torino on Saturday night.
  • Unbeaten since August, the Biancocelesti extended their lead last weekend, while Toro's winless streak reached four straight games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:23.

Still leading the pack in Serie A, surprise Scudetto challengers Lazio will visit mid-table Torino on Saturday night.

Unbeaten since August, the Biancocelesti extended their lead last weekend, while Toro's winless streak reached four straight games.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, Lazio sit three points above reigning champions Inter and two clear of city rivals Roma after storming through their first dozen games.

Having begun Gennaro Gattuso's reign with a shock Coppa Italia loss to Mantova, the Biancocelesti have since gone up through the gears, only dropping four points in Serie A so far.

Victory this week would take them onto 11 wins from 13 games, and the last team to make such a fast start was Napoli in the 2022-23 campaign, when they ultimately went on to win the title.

Lazio's most recent success, against Lecce, featured goals from two of their star players this term, as Tijjani Noslin bagged a brace before Davide Frattesi capped things off with a cheeky chip from outside the box.

Ahead of next month's Derby della Capitale, in which top spot could well be at stake, fans may even be dreaming of a first Scudetto for 27 years.

However, Gattuso will not look any further than Saturday's trip north to Turin, where Lazio have won half of their last 22 Serie A games against Torino.

That stated, the capital club did not prevail when they last met in March, as Torino won 2-0 at Stadio Olimpico Grande.

So, the hosts can now seek back-to-back victories over Lazio for the first time since 2013, even if current form suggests they may fail.

While their Roman rivals are flying high, Toro have endured an uneven season under new boss Ignazio Abate: following a slow start, they then posted three consecutive wins, before slipping back down the table.

After last week's 1-0 loss to Napoli, Abate's side have picked up just one point from their last four matches, leaving them closer to the drop zone than Italy's top six.

While leaving Naples with anything is always a tough task, they cannot expect to thrive when they return to Turin.

Not only have the Granata conceded an average of nearly two goals per game there this season, but they are also on a record run of 11 Serie A home games without a clean sheet.

With only the league to consider, Gattuso has generally stuck to a similar Lazio lineup, but he is at the moment missing two regular starters.

Though defensive duo Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo are both sidelined with flexor injuries, captain Mattia Zaccagni has resumed full training and could be named on the bench.

While Frattesi is the visitors' top scorer with five Serie A goals, Noslin has notched at least one goal involvement in all of his last four matches.

Torino have been less potent this term, but Che Adams has four top-flight strikes and Giovanni Simeone must love playing his father's old club - the Argentinian has previously scored 10 league goals against Lazio.

Ardian Ismajli limped out of the loss to Napoli with an adductor injury and has subsequently undergone surgery, while Abate has fitness doubts about wing-backs Rafik Belghali and Ricardo Rodriguez.

As Belghali is still suffering with knee inflammation, Zakaria Aboukhlal, Nicolo Fortini or even Nathan Patterson could fill in on the hosts' right flank.

Torino possible starting lineup:.

Perri; Comuzzo, Coco, Comert; Aboukhlal, Braganca, Mandragora, Vlasic, Cacciamani; Adams, Simeone.

Lazio possible starting lineup:.

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Doekhi, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin.

Well acquainted from their Milan days, Gattuso and Abate will be foes for 90 minutes this weekend, when Lazio should continue their long unbeaten run.

As Torino struggle to keep clean sheets, the league leaders are sure to score, and they have conceded under one goal per game so far this term.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

City drew 2-2 with Basingstoke Town last Saturday – and the two goals they conceded came when they were playing against ten men.

That was after Kristian Shevchenko – son of one-time Ballon D’or winner Andriy – was sent off in the first half.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Chi coach Darin Killpartrick credited Basingstoke with making it difficult for his team by changing shape when they went down to ten men.

But he mentioned he was disappointed by the way City defended for the two they let in – and it had to be viewed as an opportunity for three points passed up.

Chi are back at Oaklands Park this Saturday and it’s leaders Uxbridge who are the visitors.

Uxbridge handed City their biggest defeat of the season to date at home in mid-September – it finished 5-0 in Middlesex. And Killpartrick has warned Chi will need to be at their very best to try to get anything out of the game.

Will Sweet and Emmett Dunn were the scorers against Basingstoke as City led 1-0 and 2-1.

Killpartrick noted: “It was a missed opportunity for the win against a team who ended with ten men; however when they went down to ten, they changed to a shape that was very difficult to break down.

“We cannot defend – as a team – like we did for their two goals.

“Their first goal upset me the most. Their player has weaved around four or five players and from us that’s not the level we need to produce.

“If you defend like that at this level of football, you will get punished – particularly if you are playing top teams like that.

“But we’ve had a look at it and talked it through with the players and they know we need to defend better than that.”.

One major relief for City is that their long run of Tuesday night matches is over, at least for now.

Killpartrick said the relentless schedule since September had stretched their small squad to the limit and it was great to have a Tuesday when they could concentrate on training, and having a bit of fun as a group too.

Another boost is that two key players – midfielder Lloyd Rowlatt and defender Curtis Da Costa – are fit again and pushing for spots. James Sweet has trained again after a hamstring injury.

A major crowd is hoped for on Saturday, Killpartrick saying: “You’ll see two good teams trying to play entertaining football – we hope for plenty of support.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 14:21.

The Scottish Premiership's second and third-placed sides will meet on Saturday, when Rangers welcome Falkirk to Ibrox Stadium.

The hosts are second in the Scottish Premiership standings with 33 points, one point behind leaders Celtic, while the visitors are third with 24 points from 14 matches.

Rangers head into Saturday's match with their sights set on moving to the top of the Scottish Premiership standings for the first time this season.

The Gers trail leaders Celtic by just one point, meaning a victory would lift them above their Old Firm rivals, at least until the Bhoys take on Hearts on Sunday afternoon.

Derek McInnes' men will be full of confidence of claiming all three points, with Rangers heading into the matchday 15 fixture enjoying a sensational 14-game unbeaten run across all competitions.

In the league, Rangers have won 10 and drawn two matches during that run, including winning each of their last three Scottish Premiership fixtures, beating St Mirren 2-0, Motherwell 2-1 and Aberdeen 3-2.

The Gers are also looking to extend their superb record at Ibrox, having won all of their last nine home games, scoring 22 and conceding just four goals in that time.

Despite their fantastic form coming into this match, Rangers will expect a tough test against visitors Falkirk, who travel to Ibrox off the back of six consecutive league triumphs.

That run includes particularly notable wins against Celtic (2-0) and Hearts (5-2), and the Bairns will now be looking to add Rangers' scalp to their collection.

Thanks to those six victories, Falkirk have rapidly ascended to third in the Scottish Premiership standings with 24 points from 14 matches, although they only lead Hearts - who have played one game fewer - by one point.

Alongside their impressive recent run, Falkirk will draw further self belief from their formidable record on the road this season, recording three wins, three draws and suffering just one loss away from home in the league.

John McGlynn's side have, however, failed to defeat Rangers in any of their last seven encounters, including a 2-1 defeat earlier this season.

Rangers Scottish Premiership form:.

Rangers form (all competitions):.

Falkirk Scottish Premiership form:.

Rangers are set to be without Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Jose Cifuentes, Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti due to ongoing injuries, while Ross McCrorie is also a doubt with a hamstring injury.

Ryan Don Naderi is Rangers' top scorer in the league with seven goals, and the forward should continue just behind Kevin Kelsy in the forward line.

Falkirk are also contending with several injury absences, including Aidan Nesbitt, Aodhan Doherty, Brad Spencer, Leon McCann and Ryan Strain, while Ethan Laidlaw is a doubt to feature.

Jacob Murrell is Falkirk's top scorer with eight league goals, including seven in his last seven appearances, and the forward will start just ahead of Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames in attack.

Rangers possible starting lineup:.

Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Neil; Bouanani, Naderi, Gassama; Kelsy.

Falkirk possible starting lineup:.

Bain; McMillan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Krauhaus, Melniks; Ross, Barbrook, Eames; Murrell.

Recent findings suggest that both teams head into this match in fantastic form, leading us to expect a hard-fought encounter. However, given Rangers' formidable Ibrox form and their recent upperhand in this fixture, we are predicting a victory for the hosts.

#221281. An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 120m • 📚 Deep Dive (24081 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 120 min read (24081 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~120 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2.
  • The bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2.
  • Conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

The bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2. The adverse effects of climate change on crop productivity have historically been underestimated5. With the average global temperature expected to increase by 1.5–2.0 °C by 2050, the frequency and severity of drought events will be further increased, which could be accompanied by 30–40% reductions in food production3,4. Despite facing the greatest food-security challenges in the modern era7,8, annual crop yield improvement rates have not kept pace with projected food demands, that is, a 50–70% increase to accommodate approximately 9.8 billion people worldwide by 2050 (ref. 9), further compounding the effects of disaster events and decreasing availability of arable land.

Conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12. Increasingly precise genetic modification strategies have advanced crop engineering for drought resistance13,14,15,16,17. For example, heterologous expression of a rice trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase in developing maize ears improves yield under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions in the field16. In cassava, expressing a modified Arabidopsis potassium (K+) channel in vascular tissues improves K+ transport, photosynthesis and root biomass, allowing enhanced productivity in nutrient-poor and drought-prone environments17. However, genetic modification usually cannot provide a single, universal solution to multifactorial drought stress, and this approach frequently fails to improve yields in the field13,18 because drought resistance is a complex quantitative trait involving a multitude of small-effect loci or genes mediating diverse stress responses, such as stomatal closure (for reduced transpiration) or modified root architecture (for enhanced water uptake)10,19. Drought resistance typically accompanies trade-offs by way of reduced yield in the absence of stress6,20, undermining the effectiveness of certain genetic modification strategies. Therefore, of the genes identified in controlled conditions that often show limited effects in real-world environments, relatively few undergo rigorous field trials to properly demonstrate consistent agronomic value21.

Among known genetic resources for drought resistance, lichens have been generally overlooked despite their ubiquitous distribution across extreme ecological niches. In arid-adapted lichens, mycobionts appear to contribute more to survival under water deficit than photobionts22,23. We have previously isolated the lichen-forming fungus Endocarpon pusillum, which has extreme drought resistance. Exposure to dehydration stress identified 1,781 differentially expressed E. pusillum genes24. Through mining those data, here we identified the transcription factor gene EpTFIIAγ that broadly enhances yield and biomass production under field conditions when heterologously expressed in the world’s top-three-produced staple cereal crops of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.). EpTFIIAγ delays plant senescence, enhances photosynthetic capacity, water-use efficiency (WUE) and drought resistance by functioning as a transcriptional co-factor to coordinately target multiple genes and pathways. EpTFIIAγ binds to TATA-box-containing motifs and interacts with several endogenous wheat transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance networks involved in stress responses, plant development, photosynthesis and grain yield. Our results provide an unprecedented broad-spectrum resource for crop improvement and highlight the untapped potential of lichen mycobionts as sources of versatile transgenes for biotechnology.

Among 25 differentially expressed genes predicted to encode transcription factors identified under dehydration stress in E. pusillum (Fig. 1a), EPUS02736 exhibits the strongest upregulation and encodes a transcription initiation factor IIA γ-chain (designated EpTFIIAγ). EpTFIIAγ shares homology with TFIIAs from plants, such as Arabidopsis, wheat, rice and maize, although the genetic relatedness between EpTFIIAγ and these homologues is relatively distant (Fig. 1b). Strong expression under dehydration stress implicates EpTFIIAγ in drought adaptation of the lichen mycobiont. Towards understanding its functionality, EpTFIIAγ was expressed in the yeast ∆hog1 mutant (deficient in HOG1, which encodes the high osmolarity glycerol 1 protein kinase), resulting in remarkably enhanced growth on solid synthetic dropout (SD) −Ura medium with 0.75 M sorbitol (Fig. 1c), and statistically significantly higher growth in corresponding liquid medium than the control (Fig. 1d). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ contributes to regulating osmotic stress.

a, RNA-seq analysis of 25 transcription factor genes in E. pusillum under osmotic stress. FC, fold change; FPKM, fragments per kilobase of transcript per million mapped fragments. b, Phylogenetic analysis of EpTFIIAγ (red) and homologues from Arabidopsis, rice, maize and wheat. Bootstrap values are shown at the nodes and branch lengths are indicated by the scale bar. c,d, Osmotic stress resistance of ∆hog1 yeast expressing TFIIAγ from E. pusillum, wheat and Arabidopsis on SD−Ura medium ± 0.75 M sorbitol (c) and time course of culture density (d). n = 4 biological replicates. e, Transgene expression (top left), rosette morphology (bottom left) and survival (right) of Arabidopsis Col-0 and EpTFIIAγ lines under well-watered (WW) and drought-stress (DS) conditions. Anti-EpTFIIAγ and β-actin were used for immunoblotting. n = 3 independent experiments. Scale bars, 2 cm. f–j, Transgene expression, plant morphology and survival under WW and DS conditions in five wheat cultivars and their corresponding EpTFIIAγ lines: Fielder (f), XN979 (g), XN511 (h), JM22 (i) and XZ9104 (j). n = 3 (f) and 4 (g–j) independent experiments. Images were acquired before water withdrawal and after 3 days of rewatering following approximately 25 days of drought treatment. Scale bars, 2 cm. k,l, Field images of wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ transgenic wheat under full-irrigation (k) and water-limited (l) conditions. Scale bars, 10 cm. TL, transgenic line. m,n, Grain yield per plot under full-irrigation (m) and water-limited (n) conditions. n = 4 plots. Data are mean ± s.d. Statistical significance was assessed using two-sided Student’s t-test (d), Brown–Forsythe and Welch analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by two-sided Dunnett’s T3 test (e–j), and one-way ANOVA followed by two-sided Dunnett’s test (m,n). *P < 0.05 and **P < 0.01 indicate statistically significant differences. Gel source data are shown in Supplementary Fig. 25.

To determine whether EpTFIIAγ could also enhance drought resistance in plants, we first expressed endogenous TFIIAγ genes from Arabidopsis and wheat in the yeast hog1 mutant; however, no obvious effect on osmotic stress tolerance was observed (Fig. 1c), suggesting that TFIIAγ genes probably mediate divergent biological functions between plants and E. pusillum. We then generated three genetically independent transgenic Arabidopsis lines (TL1–TL3) constitutively and heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ and examined drought resistance. To our surprise, seedlings expressing EpTFIIAγ had survival rates approximately seven times higher than wild-type Col-0 controls under drought-stress conditions (Fig. 1e). This improved drought resistance was not limited to the eudicot Arabidopsis. Transgenic wheat cv. Fielder seedlings heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ from the strong and constitutive Ubiquitin promoter showed an approximately 3.5-fold increase in survival rate compared with wild-type Fielder under drought stress (Fig. 1f). However, overexpression of endogenous AtTFIIAγ or TaTFIIAγ in their respective native hosts had no such positive effect on drought resistance (Extended Data Fig. 1a–f), supporting their functional divergence from EpTFIIAγ. Analysis of key drought-resistance traits, including root architecture and biomass production (Extended Data Fig. 1g–o), stomatal density and aperture, and leaf water loss and transpiration (that is, leaf temperature; Extended Data Fig. 1p–u and Supplementary Fig. 1), suggested that the enhanced drought resistance among EpTFIIAγ transgenic Arabidopsis and wheat lines was mainly attributable to enhanced root growth and decreased stomatal aperture and transpiration compared with wild-type controls. Transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat seedlings over-accumulated abscisic acid, auxin and salicylic acid hormones than wild-type Fielder plants under drought stress, whereas their accumulation remained comparable with that of controls under well-watered conditions (Supplementary Fig. 2).

According to recent reports, drought resistance varies widely across wheat germplasm25. To understand whether EpTFIIAγ can endow major commercially relevant wheat cultivars in China with enhanced drought resistance, we generated four genetically independent transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines in each of cvs. Xinong979 (XN979), Xinong511 (XN511), Jimai22 (JM22) and Xingzi9104 (XZ9104), which show different degrees of stress resistance and yield25,26. Greenhouse drought-resistance assays revealed that survival rates were 2–3 times higher for transgenic lines than corresponding wild-type controls (Fig. 1g–j), whereas stomatal aperture, leaf water loss rates and transpiration were also decreased in transgenic lines under drought stress (Supplementary Figs. 3 and 4). Therefore, heterologous EpTFIIAγ expression consistently endowed drought resistance and key physiological changes across four additional wheat cultivars. EpTFIIAγ plants also displayed broad-spectrum resilience to heat stress, lodging and multiple races of the major wheat stripe-rust fungal pathogen Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Extended Data Fig. 2), further supporting potential EpTFIIAγ deployment for engineering stacked resistance to environmental stressors in wheat.

Sources indicate that certain transgenes are known to improve resistance to drought stress but at the undesirable expense of reduced plant growth or productivity, known as yield drag13,18,20. We examined performance of all five sets of transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat lines to identify potential yield drag in 3-year field trials under full-irrigation and water-limited conditions with a rain shelter in Yangling, China, which is characterized by a warm temperate semi-humid and semi-arid climate with 200–400 mm of rainfall during the growing season (Supplementary Fig. 5). All tested EpTFIIAγ lines had consistently increased grain yield across different genetic backgrounds and years compared with respective wild-type controls under full-irrigation control conditions. This increase was more pronounced under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1k–n; Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6–9). In 2025, grain yields surpassed that of the two previous years under water-limited conditions for EpTFIIAγ lines because of the higher temperature, lower rainfall and severe drought stress (Supplementary Fig. 5). Across all five backgrounds, EpTFIIAγ lines displayed 7.6–13.9% increases in grain yield per plant and 7.9–13.5% increases in yield per plot relative to controls under full-irrigation conditions, and increases of 22.3–38.3% in yield per plant and 19.4–32.8% higher yield per plot under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Fig. 7c,i). EpTFIIAγ lines were taller, had increased plant biomass, grain length, grain width and grain weight relative to respective wild-type controls, potentially contributing to increased plot yields. Despite higher grain yields, EpTFIIAγ plants had similar straw weight compared with wild-type plants, resulting in 6.1–14.8% higher harvest indices (that is, ratio of grain yield to aboveground biomass) under full irrigation and 7.6–15.5% increases in harvest indices under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). Growth duration was similar between genotypes under full irrigation, whereas time to maturity was 2–5 days longer for EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than maturation time in the wild-type under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Fig. 7f,l), reflecting adaptation to drought stress.

In a recent development, to evaluate trait stability, additional field trials were conducted in 2025 in three arid growing regions in China (Heyang, Shaanxi; Linfen, Shanxi; and Cangzhou, Hebei) with rainfall of 120–250 mm during the growing season. Grain yield per plant for EpTFIIAγ lines increased by 10.9–25.6% compared with wild-type controls, with the highest yield increases (15.6–25.6%) observed in Heyang (Supplementary Tables 4–6). These results underscored the potential of EpTFIIAγ as a valuable genetic resource for developing drought-resistant, high-yield wheat varieties in elite backgrounds regardless of water availability. In detail, EpTFIIAγ plants had expanded flag leaves, accelerated grain filling, larger pericarp cells, higher starch granule density and increased starch biosynthesis relative to wild-type controls under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Extended Data Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. 10). This accelerated filling led to heavier grains beginning at 5 days after flowering, regardless of water conditions, resulting in 3.3–8.8% greater final grain weight in well-watered EpTFIIAγ plants and 15.2–21.4% higher grain weight in drought-stressed transgenic plants than in their respective wild-type controls (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). These improvements were consistent with the higher sucrose, glucose and fructose levels, as well as increased sucrose synthase, cell-wall invertase and ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase activities observed in EpTFIIAγ grains during the early filling stage (Extended Data Fig. 4). Conversely, flag-leaf sheaths of EpTFIIAγ plants had lower levels of these sugars than wild-type controls. These results suggested that the extended duration and enhanced rate of grain filling may be key determinants of increased final grain weight and yield in EpTFIIAγ plants.

Given the drought resistance and yield boosts endowed by EpTFIIAγ in transgenic wheat lines, we examined which physiological processes are altered. EpTFIIAγ plants had delayed senescence compared with controls under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9), which we hypothesized might be due to increased WUE. We also hypothesised that carbon assimilation might be altered given that increases in yield and biomass require enhanced carbon fixation. To examine possible differences in water status and carbon assimilation between wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ plants, we first used plant multispectral imaging to estimate normalized difference vegetation index and normalized water index values at seedling stage in a growth chamber. Transgenic plants indeed had higher normalized difference vegetation index and lower normalized water index values than Fielder plants under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 11). EpTFIIAγ seedling leaves had lower 13C fractionation than Fielder during the 18 days of drought treatment following water withdrawal (Fig. 2a), indicating enhanced WUE in these transgenic plants. These results are consistent with the lower water loss rate and transpiration for EpTFIIAγ plants under drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 1p–u).

Recent findings suggest that to further assess the effects of EpTFIIAγ expression on carbon assimilation, we measured quantum yield of photosystem II photochemistry (ΦPSII). Transgenic EpTFIIAγ seedlings had approximately 14.6% higher ΦPSII than Fielder control plants under well-watered conditions, and approximately 29.9% greater ΦPSII under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ expression led to enhanced maintenance of PSII activity. EpTFIIAγ plants had improved light–response and CO2–response curves of net photosynthesis (Fig. 2b,c). In addition, the abundance of PSI, PSII, cytochrome b6/f and LHC proteins, as well as RuBisCO subunits were all increased in transgenic plants under well-watered or drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5d). RuBisCO activity was increased in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 5c), which agreed with A–Ci curves showing higher maximum rates of RuBisCO carboxylation and electron transport (Extended Data Fig. 5e–h). Consistent with these increases, EpTFIIAγ leaves over-accumulated sucrose, glucose, starch and soluble sugars (Extended Data Fig. 5i), further demonstrating enhanced carbon assimilation in these plants. Of note, drought stress triggered a marked accumulation of root soluble sugars (for example, sucrose, glucose and fructose) in EpTFIIAγ plants compared with Fielder, whereas no such difference was observed under optimal conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5j), aligning with enhanced root growth under drought stress.

We next evaluated how EpTFIIAγ contributes to lifting photosynthetic capacity in field-grown plants. Chlorophyll content (soil and plant analyser development, SPAD), maximum quantum yield of PSII photochemistry (Fv/Fm) and photosynthetic rate were all enhanced in EpTFIIAγ transgenic plants in all five wheat cultivars compared with their corresponding wild-type controls at all of the tillering, stem elongation, flowering and milk development stages under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 12–17). However, stomatal conductance and transpiration rate were lower in transgenic plants under water-limited conditions, although some EpTFIIAγ lines had slightly higher stomatal conductance under full-irrigation conditions. In agreement with these results, WUE (that is, the ratio of net photosynthetic rate to transpiration rate) was improved in EpTFIIAγ plants under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 14–17). Under full-irrigation field conditions, no obvious phenotypic changes in root development were seen between wild-type Fielder and transgenic plants. By contrast, all EpTFIIAγ lines had increased root length and biomass compared with Fielder under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2h–j), aligning with the stay-green phenotype observed in shoots (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9). Together, field-grown EpTFIIAγ wheat lines have enhanced WUE, resulting in slower water consumption, delayed senescence under water-limited conditions, and consequently more extensive root development, thereby facilitating greater water uptake. These data also suggested that enhanced photosynthetic capacity and CO2 assimilation contributed to the increased biomass and grain yield observed in EpTFIIAγ wheat plants.

In a recent development, eukaryotic transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) requires numerous general transcription factors and cofactors to nucleate at core promoter sites, which typically contain several DNA sequence elements (for example, TATA boxes), to form the pre-initiation complex27. Among them, the transcription initiation factor TFIIA is a general cofactor that acts as an anti-repressor or co-activator27,28. In multicellular eukaryotes, the TFIIA complex typically comprises α-subunit, β-subunit and γ-subunit, encoded by TFIIAαβ and TFIIAγ genes27,29. To characterize the function of EpTFIIAγ, we first examined TFIIAγ sequences across species. EpTFIIAγ retains a conserved protein architecture while also harbouring a unique, lineage-specific N-terminal extension (Supplementary Table 7 and Supplementary Fig. 18). To determine whether EpTFIIAγ participates in transcription initiation, we first examined its subcellular localization in wheat protoplasts. EpTFIIAγ–GFP mainly localized to the nucleus, whereas intact TaTFIIAγ–GFP and AtTFIIAγ–GFP fusions showed both nuclear and cytoplasmic localization (Extended Data Fig. 6a,b). To investigate whether EpTFIIAγ could interact with endogenous TFIIAαβ to form the TFIIA holocomplex in plants, we conducted yeast two-hybrid, luciferase-complementation imaging and pulldown assays. These experiments consistently demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ fails to detectably interact with either wheat or Arabidopsis TFIIAαβ, whereas both TaTFIIAγ and AtTFIIAγ could interact with their corresponding TFIIAαβ proteins to form complete TFIIA complexes (Extended Data Fig. 6c–g). These results indicated that EpTFIIAγ does not appear to function as a transcription initiation factor in plants, or at least does so differently from these expression hosts.

In a recent development, the TFIIA recognition element (IIARE) located upstream of the TATA box enhances recruitment of TFIIA and other components to activate transcription at TATA-box promoter motifs27,29. We asked whether EpTFIIAγ could similarly bind to such recognition sites. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could indeed directly bind to an IIARE-containing TATA box, whereas neither wheat TaTFIIAγ nor Arabidopsis AtTFIIAγ displayed detectable binding (Extended Data Fig. 6h,i). Although fungal and plant TFIIAγ proteins share conserved α-helical and β-sheet architectures, EpTFIIAγ uniquely harbours an N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR; Fig. 3a). Hypothesizing that this region may confer specialized biological function, we generated an IDR deletion variant (EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR)). This truncation did not bind to IIARE-containing TATA-box fragments, and likewise, its nuclear localization was impaired (Fig. 3b,c and Extended Data Fig. 6j). Conversely, fusing the EpTFIIAγ-derived IDR to TaTFIIAγ or AtTFIIAγ conferred binding to probes carrying an IIARE-containing TATA box (Fig. 3b and Extended Data Fig. 6j).

According to recent reports, to test whether this IDR could drive liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), we expressed EpTFIIAγ–GFP in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells. Upon hyperosmotic stress, EpTFIIAγ maintained a homogeneous nuclear distribution and did not coalesce into condensates under either stress or non-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 19a). Moreover, His–EpTFIIAγ did not detectably form dynamic droplets in vitro, indicating that its relatively short IDR was insufficient to trigger LLPS (Supplementary Fig. 19b). Further evaluation of chromatin-binding dynamics through fluorescence recovery after photobleaching and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy indicated that EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) exhibited markedly shallower bleach depth and accelerated recovery kinetics (Fig. 3c and Supplementary Fig. 19c–h), indicating attenuated chromatin association and higher mobility than full-length control. Stable-transgenic EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) expression in wheat cv. Fielder conferred no obvious improvement in drought resistance relative to wild-type (Extended Data Fig. 6k–m), indicating that the IDR is indeed indispensable for EpTFIIAγ function in the drought-stress response.

Recent findings suggest that to identify EpTFIIAγ-binding sites across the wheat genome, we performed chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP–seq) with transgenic plants stably expressing EpTFIIAγ–HA in the cv. Fielder (Fig. 3d). Across two replicates, 17,131 putative EpTFIIAγ-binding sites were identified, 85% of which are in intergenic regions and 15% in genic regions, including gene bodies as well as the 3-kb upstream and 300-bp downstream flanking sequences presumed to harbour the promoter and transcriptional terminator, respectively (Fig. 3e). Analysis of 2,570 genic binding sites identified 1,347 annotated genes bound by EpTFIIAγ–HA (Fig. 3f and Supplementary Table 8), and the core motif within these binding regions was enriched with a TATA-containing element (Fig. 3g). Gene Ontology analysis found that these EpTFIIAγ–HA target genes were enriched in terms related to stress responses, such as ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’, ‘response to cold’, ‘regulation of stomatal movement’ and ‘transpiration’; hormone responses, such as ‘response to abscisic acid (ABA)’, ‘response to auxin’ and ‘response to brassinosteroid’, as well as ‘photosynthesis’ and ‘chlorophyll biosynthesis’ (Fig. 3h). Further EMSAs confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could bind to promoter regions of 387 wheat genes, underscoring its capacity to regulate diverse biological pathways in planta, such as those related to stress response, development, photosynthesis and yield formation (Extended Data Fig. 7a, Supplementary Table 9 and Supplementary Fig. 20).

To define the regulatory network involved in the effects of EpTFIIAγ on photosynthetic efficiency, WUE and the drought-stress response, we compared transcriptomes of 20-day-old wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ transgenic seedlings. This identified 1,953 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; fold change of more than 2 or less than 0.5, P < 0.05) in transgenic plants relative to Fielder, including 1,405 upregulated and 548 downregulated DEGs (Extended Data Fig. 7b–g and Supplementary Table 10). By examining overlap between ChIP–seq and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, we identified 1,056 candidate target genes that are potentially bound and transcriptionally regulated by EpTFIIAγ, including 824 upregulated and 232 downregulated genes in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 8a,b). Among them, stress-response-related genes involved in ABA and drought responses showed strong enrichment (Extended Data Fig. 8c), such as wheat homologues of Arabidopsis MYBR1 (ref. 30), FBH4 (ref. 31) and DREB1C32 (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10). Other genes known to function in plant development, source–sink partitioning and grain yield were also present among upregulated DEGs, including the CONSTANS-like gene TaCol-B5 (ref. 33), wheat homologues of rice OsCIN2 (ref. 34) and OsSWEET4 (ref. 35), and homologues of Arabidopsis VND7 (ref. 36) and SWEET12 (ref. 37). Among photosynthesis-related DEGs, we found TaYCF9 and TaCP47, which are homologues of Arabidopsis PsbZ38 and CP47 (ref. 39) encoding subunits of the PSII reaction centre. In addition, we identified TaCOG1, a homologue of the Arabidopsis Dof transcription factor COG1, that promotes biomass accumulation by enhancing photosynthetic capacity40. TaGAPC1, a redox-dependent regulator of energy metabolism that mediates stress responses in Arabidopsis41, was also upregulated (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10).

Industry observers note that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could bind in vitro to approximately 30-bp promoter fragments containing TATA motifs from TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1, and this interaction could be compromised by competition from unlabelled probes (Fig. 3i, Extended Data Fig. 8d and Supplementary Fig. 21a). ChIP–quantitative PCR (qPCR) indicated that these promoter fragments showed greater enrichment in EpTFIIAγ–HA genomic DNA precipitated by anti-haemagglutinin antibody than by the immunoglobulin G (IgG) control (Fig. 3j and Extended Data Fig. 8e), demonstrating that EpTFIIAγ could indeed bind to TATA-containing core promoter motifs. In dual-luciferase reporter assays using approximately 1.5-kb promoter fragments, activities of target promoters were upregulated in the presence of EpTFIIAγ compared with empty vector controls (Fig. 3k, Extended Data Fig. 8f and Supplementary Fig. 21b), supported by real-time (RT)–qPCR analyses revealing that TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 mRNAs were all expressed at higher levels in all three EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than in wild-type Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 8g). These results collectively indicated that EpTFIIAγ functions as a transcriptional cofactor to regulate target gene expression.

It has been revealed that to determine how downstream regulatory targets contribute to enhancing drought resistance, photosynthetic efficiency and grain yield in EpTFIIAγ plants, we generated transgenic wheat lines overexpressing TaDREB1C, TaCOG1 or TaCIN2 in the cv. Fielder background. TaDREB1C lines had enhanced drought resistance and WUE through accelerated stomatal closure and reduced transpiration compared with Fielder under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 9a–g). This overexpression did not detectably alter growth period, which remained comparable with controls under full irrigation (Extended Data Fig. 9h–j). Plants overexpressing TaCOG1 had enhanced photosynthetic and carbon-fixation capacities, resulting in increased biomass and grain yield relative to controls (Extended Data Fig. 9k–p). Moreover, TaCIN2 overexpression resulted in accelerated grain filling, ultimately increasing grain size and yield (Extended Data Fig. 9q–v). These results position the EpTFIIAγ regulon as pivotal for concurrently improving drought resilience and yield potential in wheat.

Sources indicate that to investigate the mechanisms through which EpTFIIAγ drives enhanced drought resistance, photosynthetic capacity and grain yield, we conducted yeast two-hybrid screening using a cDNA library obtained from wheat cv. Chinese Spring seedlings. Four successive rounds of screening with EpTFIIAγ serving as bait yielded 112 candidate interacting proteins (Supplementary Table 11), including 22 putative transcription factors. After repeating yeast two-hybrid assays to confirm that EpTFIIAγ could interact with wheat homologues of Arabidopsis transcriptional activators WRKY46 (ref. 42), AKS1 (ref. 43), ARF6 (ref. 44) and VOZ1 (ref. 45) (Fig. 4a), luciferase-complementation imaging tested whether EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these partners. Co-expression of EpTFIIAγ–C-terminal luciferase fragment (cLUC) with N-terminal luciferase fragment (nLUC)–TaWRKY46, nLUC–TaAKS1, nLUC–TaARF6 or nLUC–TaVOZ1 produced chemiluminescence, whereas no signal was observed in regions infiltrated with vector controls (Fig. 4b). Bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays further highlighted that co-expression of the EpTFIIAγ–cYFP with nYFP–TaWRKY46, nYFP–TaAKS1, nYFP–TaARF6 or nYFP–TaVOZ1 led to obvious YFP signal (Fig. 4c and Supplementary Fig. 22a,b). Pulldown assays indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could interact with GST–TaWRKY46, GST–TaAKS1, GST–TaARF6 and HA–TaVOZ1 in vitro (Fig. 4d). Co-immunoprecipitation assays in N. benthamiana leaves co-expressing 35Spro:GFP–EpTFIIAγ and 35Spro:mCherry–TaWRKY46, 35Spro:mCherry–TaARF6 or 35Spro:mCherry–EpTFIIAγ with 35Spro:GFP–TaAKS1, 35Spro:GFP–TaVOZ1 also confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these transcription factors in planta (Fig. 4e). By contrast, the IDR-deleted EpTFIIAγ variant failed to detectably interact with any tested partners (Supplementary Fig. 22c,d), highlighting the essential role of this IDR. Moreover, no interactions were observed between wheat TaTFIIAγ and the transcription factors TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1 (Supplementary Fig. 22e,f), underscoring EpTFIIAγ functional specificity.

To map genome-wide binding sites and target genes, we used CUT&Tag in stable-transgenic cv. Fielder plants expressing TaWRKY46–HA, TaAKS1–FLAG, TaARF6–HA or TaVOZ1–HA. Integrative analysis identified 467, 309, 495 and 505 target genes that are potentially co-bound and co-regulated by EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, respectively (Supplementary Table 12 and Supplementary Fig. 23), suggesting direct involvement in the EpTFIIAγ regulatory network. GST–TaWRKY46 could bind in vitro to probes containing the W-box from the TaCol-B5, TaSWEET4 and TaSWEET12 promoters, and these binding events increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Similarly, GST–TaAKS1 could bind to probes harbouring the G-box or E-box from the TaDREB1C, TaCol-B5, TaYCF9 or TaCOG1 promoter regions, with the addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ markedly strengthening these interactions in vitro. Moreover, GST–TaARF6 could interact with AuxRE-containing probes derived from the TaYCF9, TaFBH4 and TaCIN2 promoters, which was boosted by addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ, whereas GST–TaVOZ1 bound to probes with a 5′-CTTCTT-3′ motif present in the TaCP47, TaVND7, TaMYBR1 and TaGAPC1 promoter regions, which also increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Dual-luciferase reporter assays indicated that TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 could activate genes with corresponding promoter recognition sites (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b).

In a recent development, to determine whether EpTFIIAγ functions coordinately with or independently of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 in regulating target genes, we performed dual-luciferase reporter assays. Upon co-expressing EpTFIIAγ with each respective transcription factor, LUC activity driven by the TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 promoters was greater than the expression of wheat transcription factors alone (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b). To clarify whether activation of these transcription-factor genes contributed to the observed drought resistance of transgenic EpTFIIAγ plants, we examined drought resistance in lines overexpressing TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 (Extended Data Fig. 11a–d), as well as wrky46-knockout and arf6-knockout mutants by gene editing in cv. Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 11e,f). All overexpression lines had enhanced drought resistance relative to Fielder, whereas both mutants had compromised drought resistance compared with Fielder controls (Extended Data Fig. 11g–j). To further characterize the genetic interactions of EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1, we crossed EpTFIIAγ plants (Fielder background) with each overexpression line. Under normal conditions, homozygous double-transgene-positive progeny of all crosses bore phenotypes comparable with that of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 overexpression plants. By contrast, double-transgene-carrying hybrids showed stronger drought resistance than control plants expressing a single transgene (Extended Data Fig. 11k,l). These findings collectively demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with select transcription activators, such as TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, and that their interactions resulted in additive effects on EpTFIIAγ target gene expression, consequently enhancing the drought response, photosynthesis and grain yield.

To determine whether EpTFIIAγ function in conferring drought resistance was conserved in other major cereal crops, we generated three transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines each in rice cv. Nipponbare and maize inbred line B73 backgrounds (Fig. 5a,b). In greenhouse drought-resistance assays, survival of transgenic EpTFIIAγ rice and maize lines was extended by approximately 2.6-fold and approximately 2.8-fold for rice (Fig. 5c,d) and maize (Fig. 5e,f), respectively, compared with their wild-type controls. Transcriptomic analysis found that genes involved in ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to ABA’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’ and ‘photosynthesis’ were enriched among upregulated DEGs in EpTFIIAγ seedlings of both species (Extended Data Fig. 12a,b and Supplementary Tables 13 and 14).
